description: AuthDS-tier verdict meta-vectors: (actual, entry) -> grade_authds verdict. A comparator implementation is conformant iff it reproduces every `verdict`. Precedence: panicked → coal unconditionally, checked before the entry's kind or expected values are read; not-implemented → coverage (a growth-ledger cell, not coal); then value grading dispatched on entry.kind. avl_prove grades `proof` and `digest` as INDEPENDENT dimensions with no suppression between them — a digest that matches expected while the proof bytes do not is graded proof-coal/digest-nice, not suppressed to n/a, because a digest-correct/proof-wrong runner (non-canonical AVL proof bytes that still happen to reduce to the canonical digest) is the class of defect this tier exists to surface; chaining the dimensions would hide it behind a green digest. Both avl_prove dimensions additionally require actual.error to be null — a non-null error vetoes both regardless of whether the produced values happen to match expected. avl_verify grades `accepted -> results -> digest` as a CHAIN: results is graded only when proof_accepted matches expected AND expected.proof_accepted is true (there is nothing legitimate downstream to grade on a rejected proof, so results and digest are 'n/a'); digest is graded only when results is nice, because a digest computed after a divergent operation sequence carries no information and is suppressed to 'n/a' rather than compared. `new_digest_hex: null` is itself a real, meaningful value — a failing operation poisons the verifier so it reports no digest — and null-vs-null is a legitimate nice match, not an absent-field n/a. An entry kind this grader does not recognize grades coal on every dimension of the default avl_prove shape — never a silent pass.

cases.name: prove-both-nice
cases.description: avl_prove: proofs and digests both match expected exactly, error null → proof nice, digest nice.

cases.name: prove-proof-coal-digest-nice
cases.description: avl_prove: the proof bytes diverge from the canonical proof (a non-canonical serialization) while the resulting digest still matches expected. proof and digest are independent — the digest match must not suppress the proof mismatch, because a digest-correct/proof-wrong runner is precisely the defect class (non-canonical AVL proof bytes) this tier exists to catch.

cases.name: prove-both-coal-data-mismatch
cases.description: avl_prove: both the proof bytes and the digest diverge from expected → both dimensions grade coal, independently of each other.

cases.name: prove-errored-coal
cases.description: avl_prove: the runner reports an error even though the proof and digest values it produced happen to match expected byte-for-byte (stale data from a previous entry, or a partially populated actual). A non-null error must veto both dimensions regardless of value equality — a failed run is never gradeable as nice.

cases.name: verify-full-nice
cases.description: avl_verify: the proof is accepted as expected, every operation result matches, and the resulting digest matches → all three dimensions nice.

cases.name: verify-over-accept-coal
cases.description: avl_verify: the reference verifier refuses this proof (proof_accepted:false) but the runner anchors it anyway (proof_accepted:true) — an over-accept, the failure mode the reject arm exists to catch. accepted grades coal, and there is nothing legitimate downstream to grade, so results and digest are n/a rather than compared against data the reference never produced.

cases.name: verify-rejected-proof-nice
cases.description: avl_verify: both the reference and the runner refuse the proof at the same starting digest under the same settings. Reproducing a rejection is itself a nice verdict; results and digest are n/a because no operations were legitimately attempted on either side.

cases.name: verify-results-mismatch-suppresses-digest
cases.description: avl_verify: the proof is accepted on both sides, but one operation's outcome differs (ok:true vs ok:false) → results grades coal. digest is downstream of the operations, not parallel to them, so it is suppressed to n/a rather than compared — a digest computed after a divergent operation sequence carries no information.

cases.name: verify-poisoned-null-digest-nice
cases.description: avl_verify: a failing operation poisons the verifier so it reports no digest — new_digest_hex:null is a real, meaningful value here, not an absent field. Both sides poisoned identically is a correctly reproduced verdict, so digest grades nice via null-equals-null, not n/a and not coal.

cases.name: panicked
cases.description: A runner crash grades panicked unconditionally, before the entry's kind or expected values are even consulted — checked ahead of every other precedence rule.

actual.note: index out of bounds in tree rebuild

cases.name: not-implemented
cases.description: A conformer with no prover declares not-implemented rather than attempting the operation. This is a coverage/growth-ledger cell, not a coal verdict — checked after panicked but before any value grading.

cases.name: unknown-kind-coal
cases.description: An entry kind this grader does not recognize (a future or malformed kind discriminator) must never silently pass — it grades coal on every dimension of the default authds_prove shape rather than defaulting to nice.
